summary.title: Computer Security Incident Handling Guide (NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2)
summary.one_liner: NIST's guide to setting up a computer security incident response capability and handling incidents through preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident lessons learned.
takeaways: Incident response follows a life cycle: preparation, detection and analysis, containment/eradication/recovery, and post-incident activity.
Organizations need a formal incident response policy, plan, and procedures, plus a chosen team model and staffing.
Incident prioritization uses functional, information, and recoverability impact categories.
Lessons learned and retained incident data feed back into future response.
This revision is withdrawn (April 3, 2025) and superseded by NIST SP 800-61r3.
summary.summary: This is NIST Special Publication 800-61 Revision 2 (August 2012), a guide for establishing computer security incident response capabilities and handling incidents. It covers organizing a response team, the incident handling life cycle, coordination and information sharing, and scenarios and data elements in appendices. The guidance is platform-independent. The page also carries a withdrawal notice stating the document was superseded in its entirety by NIST SP 800-61r3 on April 3, 2025.
